Welder User Manual

Welder is an open-source, node-based compositor. Footage comes in through Read nodes, flows down a graph of nodes, and goes out through Write nodes. This manual covers the editor, the main workflows, and every node.

Unzip and run

Getting started

Welder needs no installer. Unzip it anywhere and double-click Welder.bat (or bin\welder_ui.exe). Every zip unpacks into the same welder-{{VERSION}}-win64 folder, so unzip them all in one place.

welder-{{VERSION}}-win64.zip Required

The editor, the command-line renderer, docs and examples.

…-python.zip .nk import

Python for importing and pasting .nk scripts. Skip it if Python 3 is installed.

…-rife-models.zip RIFE

The neural networks the RIFE retiming node uses.

…-tests.zip, …-ofx-tests.zip Optional

Engine, EXR and OFX self-tests and test plugins.

Launching

  • Welder.bat starts the editor. Drag a .weld comp or a .nk script onto it to open that file.
  • Welder-reset-workspace.bat starts with the default panel layout. The old layout is kept as layout.ini.bak.
  • try-it.bat runs the self-tests, renders the demo comps, and translates and renders the sample .nk script.
  • Help › User Manual in Welder opens this page.

Welder needs no installer. Unpack the tarballs into the same place and run ./Welder in the welder-{{VERSION}}-linux-x86_64 folder; ./install-desktop-entry.sh adds it to your applications menu.

…-linux-x86_64.tar.gz Required

The editor, the command-line renderer, docs and examples.

…-rife-models.tar.gz RIFE

The neural networks the RIFE retiming node uses.

…-tests.tar.gz Optional

Engine and EXR self-tests.

Python 3 .nk import

Install it from your distribution to import and paste .nk scripts.

Launching

  • ./Welder starts the editor; ./Welder shot010.weld opens a comp or a .nk script.
  • ./Welder --reset-workspace starts with the default panel layout. The old layout is kept as layout.ini.bak.
  • Needs glibc 2.38 or newer, OpenGL 3.3, and optionally Vulkan for GPU processing.
  • Help › User Manual in Welder opens this page.

Welder needs no installer. Unzip it and drag Welder.app to Applications. The first time, right-click it and choose Open, because this build isn't notarized yet. Use the -arm64 download on Apple silicon and -x86_64 on Intel Macs.

On a Mac, press Cmd wherever this manual says Ctrl.

Launching

  • Double-click Welder.app, or drop a .weld comp or .nk script on it.
  • open -a Welder --args --reset-workspace starts with the default panel layout. The old layout is kept as layout.ini.bak.
  • Needs macOS 11 or later. Python 3 (python.org or Homebrew) is needed for .nk import; GPU processing uses MoltenVK (brew install molten-vk).
  • Help › User Manual in Welder opens this page.

Your first comp

Read1R

1Press R over the node graph, or drag files onto the window. Numbered frames show as one sequence. On the first Read, Welder offers to match the project's frame range and resolution: press Enter.

Grade1G

2With the Read selected press 1 to view it, then G for a Grade, B for a Blur, or Tab to search every node by name.

Write1W

3Press W and set its file, for example shot_v001.####.exr. Press F5 to render all Writes, F7 for the selected ones.

Save with CtrlS. Comps are .weld files; AltShiftS saves and bumps the version to _v002.

From the command line

bin\welder.exe render examples\demo.weld -f 1-24 -v
bin\welder.exe node   examples\demo.weld Look -o look.exr -f 12
bin\welder.exe info   examples\demo.weld
bin\welder.exe nk     comp.weld -o shot.nk
bin/welder render examples/demo.weld -f 1-24 -v
bin/welder node   examples/demo.weld Look -o look.exr -f 12
bin/welder info   examples/demo.weld
bin/welder nk     comp.weld -o shot.nk
Welder.app/Contents/MacOS/welder render examples/demo.weld -f 1-24 -v
Welder.app/Contents/MacOS/welder info   examples/demo.weld
Welder.app/Contents/MacOS/welder nk     comp.weld -o shot.nk

Add --no-gpu to render on the CPU only.

Six docked panels

The workspace

File Edit Render Viewer Workspace Help
Nodes
Viewerthe viewed node's image, 2D or 3D

build the comp here
PanelWhat it's for
NodesThe toolbar: a button per node group (Image, Draw, Time, Channel, Color, Filter, Keyer, Merge, Transform, Stylize, MoGraph, 3D, Value, AI, Other, OFX).
ViewerThe viewed node's image, with the tools of the node being edited drawn on top.
TimelineScrubbing, playback, in and out points, keyframe ticks and the RAM cache line.
Node GraphWhere the comp is built. Curve Editor, Dope Sheet and Messages are tabs beside it.
PropertiesThe panels of the nodes being edited, newest on top.

Keys go to the panel under the mouse: B over the graph inserts a Blur, over the viewer it shows the blue channel.

  • Drag a panel's tab to move, dock or float it; drag the line between panels to resize them.
  • Tap Space to maximize the panel under the mouse, again to restore. A maximized Viewer keeps the Timeline under it.
  • The Workspace menu brings any panel to the front.

Layout in a mess? Use Workspace › Reset Workspace (ShiftF12): every panel, floating ones included, goes back to its default place. Welder also keeps panels reachable on its own: a panel dropped into the toolbar or timeline gets its tab back, and floating panels stay on screen and big enough to resize. If the menu is gone, start Welder with {{RESETHOW}}.

Top to bottom

The node graph

A comp is a graph read top to bottom: each node takes images in through its inputs and passes its result out of the bottom.

Create

Tab and type a name, the toolbar, or right-click. Hotkeys insert after the selection; hold Shift for a new branch.

Connect

Drag an output dot onto a node or input. Grab either end of a pipe to reconnect it, or drop it in space to disconnect. Node edges are wide grab areas.

Insert and shake

Drop a node on a pipe to insert it. Shake a node while dragging to pull it out; the chain heals.

Line up

Nodes snap so centres line up and Dots keep pipes straight. Ctrl places freely, AltShiftA auto-aligns.

Node hotkeys

KeyInsertsKeyInserts

Drag files onto the window: images and movies become Reads (a folder brings in every sequence), .nk scripts paste as nodes, .obj becomes ReadGeo, .ply ReadSplat, LUTs OCIOFileTransform, and .gizmo the gizmo.

Groups, gizmos and backdrops

  • CtrlG makes a Group with its inputs and output wired; CtrlEnter goes inside. Add knobs of its own and read them inside as parent.amount.
  • Save as gizmo keeps it in {{CFG}}{{S}}gizmos; gizmos show in Tab search, as do .gizmo files on WELDER_GIZMO_PATH.
  • Right-click › Backdrop around selection frames nodes in a coloured box that carries them. Its corner button minimises it to one node's size.
  • Animated nodes show an animation icon; nodes an import couldn't translate show red.
Look closer

The Viewer

Select a node and press 1–9 to view it in that slot; with nothing selected the number switches slots, keeping zoom and position so you can flip plate and comp on the same edge.

The toolbar holds the layer and channel menus, the display transform, A/B compare (a wipe or a difference against another slot or node), Fit, 1:1, 3D, and full res (off renders lighter when zoomed out).

RGBA Y

One channel at a time (again for RGB); Y shows luminance.

M Q

Matte as a red overlay; show or hide every overlay: roto shapes, handles, trackers, format and bbox.

, . F H

Gain down or up half a stop; fit; fill.

JKL IO

Play back, stop, play forward; set in and out points.

Proxy, caching and playback

  • CtrlP renders at the project's proxy scale. Every size in every node is in full-resolution pixels, so results match.
  • Frames ahead of the playhead render several at a time into RAM; the Timeline's green line shows what's cached, and the cache button renders the whole range.
  • Slow frames also go to the disk cache (20 GB by default), so they come back after an undo or when the comp reopens. F12 clears cached images.
  • The Timeline's range menu shows Global, Input (the viewed footage) or Custom frames. The fps readout turns red when playback falls behind.
Knobs, keys, expressions

Properties & animation

Double-click a node, or press Enter, to open its panel. Drag a number to scrub it, click to type. CtrlEnter closes the top panel, CtrlShiftA closes them all. Every node also has a Node tab: label, colour, disable and lifetime.

Keyframes

The diamond by a knob sets or deletes a key; Alt+click a value keys every part. Animated knobs turn blue and the node gets an animation icon.

Expressions

Press = over a knob. Read frame, Blur1.size, parent.amount, [value Node.knob], with sin, clamp, noise and more. Purple when driven, red on error.

Exposed knobs

Right-click a number knob › Expose as input. Anything connected there sets the knob every frame: an image, a Sample, Math, an Oscillator.

Curves and keys

Curve Editor and Dope Sheet sit beside the Node Graph: edit keys, tangents and timing, including Tracker tracks.

Value nodes that drive knobs

NodeGives
SampleAn image's value at a point, over an area or the whole frame
Value · TimeA typed or animated number · the frame × speed + offset
Math · MapRangeAdd, multiply, power, sine, wrap … · one range mapped onto another
Oscillator · CycleA wave (sine, square, saw, noise) · a repeating ramp, for X, Y and Z
Combine · CombineXYZTwo signals mixed · one value per part of an XY / XYZ knob

Example: Noise → Sample → MapRange 0–1 to 2–40 → a Blur's exposed size makes the blur breathe. CtrlZ / CtrlY undo and redo every edit.

In, through, out

Footage, colour & rendering

Reading footage

A Read loads shot.####.exr, shot.%04d.exr or a movie, with the classic Frame Range (hold, loop, bounce, black), frame offsets, Missing Frames handling, Input Transform, Premultiplied, Raw Data and a Metadata tab. Mapped network drives are stored as UNC paths so scripts open the same on every machine.

FormatReadsWrite options
EXREvery compression, multi-part, tiledhalf / float, DWAA / DWAB and more, data window
DPX · TIFF8–16-bit · up to 32-bit floatbit depth; TIFF compression
PNG, JPEG, TGA, BMP, HDRYesPNG 8 / 16-bit
MoviesProRes, DNxHD/HR, H.264, HEVC, VP9, FFV1 …ProRes to 4444 XQ, DNxHR, MJPEG, MPEG-4, FFV1, PNG

Colour management

Project Settings › Color (S over the graph) sets the OCIO config (built-in ACES or your own), the working space (ACEScg for new comps), defaults for 8–16-bit files, and the viewer's display and view. Reads and Writes each have a colour space; raw skips it.

Rendering

F5 · F7

Render all Writes, or the selected ones. A Write's own Render button works too.

Frame ranges

Input (the default), global, in–out, visible, or custom: 1040-1105, 1-100x2, 1,5,9.

Frame server

Several background processes render at once. Continue on error lists failed frames and keeps going.

GPU

Transforms, trackers, Blur, Sharpen, Defocus, ZDefocus and Denoise run on any Vulkan GPU with CPU-identical results.

Chains of Transform, Position, CornerPin2D, Tracker, PlanarTracker and WarpStabilize resample once, so stacking them doesn't soften the image.

Shapes and strokes

Roto, paint & warping

Roto (O) draws mattes and RotoPaint (P) adds strokes. Open the panel and the viewer shows a tool strip; after you finish a shape it returns to Select.

ToolKeyHow
SelectQDrag points, tangents (Ctrl breaks one) or feather; click a shape to move it; marquee
Bezier, B-spline, Ellipse, RectangleVClick to add points, drag for tangents; first point or Enter closes
Brush / EraserNPaint with the panel's colour, size, hardness; Shift-drag sizes the brush
Clone / RevealCCtrl+click sets the clone source; Reveal paints in bg1
BlurXBlurs the background where you paint

Per-point feather

Ctrl-drag a point to pull out its own feather. With several selected, pulling one feathers them all outward. E / ShiftE push it out or in.

Autokey

On by default: editing a shape keys it on the current frame. Per item: opacity, feather, blend mode, transform, lifetime.

SplineWarp

Draw source curves (A) and destination curves (B); the image bends from one to the other. Switch with edit A / edit B over the viewer.

GridWarp

Drag grid points in the viewer; Shift-drag moves the other grid. reset grids starts over.

2D, planar, 3D

Tracking

Tracker

Open the Tracker's panel: a toolbar appears over the viewer with track buttons, key, key track, clear and grab. While it tracks you watch the pattern on top of the footage, with its error (e=) and a zoom window.

Settings tab

Channels, pre-track filter, max_error, warp type (Translate up to Affine), pattern grab behaviour, keyframe tracking options.

Transform tab

Stabilize, match-move, remove or add jitter, against a reference frame, with smoothing and motion blur. Export Transform or CornerPin2D nodes.

PlanarTracker

CtrlAlt+click around a flat, textured area to draw the region, drag the surface corners onto what you want to pin, and track with ZXCV. It always compares with the reference frame, so it doesn't drift.

CameraTracker

Source+ Mask

1Connect the plate; roto anything moving on its own into Mask.

track features

2Hundreds of features are tracked through the range.

solve camera

3Tracks turn green, yellow or red by error; a good solve is well under 1 px.

scene & export

4Set ground plane, origin and scale; export a Camera, Card3D, LensDistortion, files, or a mesh from the points.

WarpStabilize steadies a whole shot like After Effects' Warp Stabilizer: press Analyse, then smooth or remove the motion.

On your GPU

AI nodes

The AI group runs on an NVIDIA GPU through the ML worker, a Python process Welder starts in the background. Press Run, keep working, and the node shows the result when it's ready.

TrackMask

Click an object; SAM 2.1 masks it and follows it through the shot. Click again where it slips.

Depth

Steady depth.Z for the whole shot (Video Depth Anything), relative or metric.

AlphaGen · LTX

A matte without a green screen; LTX-2.5 video-to-video presets such as upscale, relight and day to night.

Reconstruct

Every frame's camera, depth and a point cloud in one pass (MapAnything).

GaussianSplat · NeRF

Trained per shot from the plate and its solved camera, refining the camera.

RIFE

Neural retiming on any Vulkan GPU, without the ML worker.

Setting up (once)

Set up ML

1Installs Python, PyTorch and the model code into {{MLDIR}} (about 15 GB).

HF token

2For LTX, accept each model's licence on Hugging Face and paste a Read token.

Download

3Fetch each model the node lists, or install by hand into its folder.

Built for a 24 GB card (RTX 3090 / 4090). LTX and AlphaGen want about 64 GB of system RAM, or set weights to disk.

Screens, HUDs, glitches

Motion graphics

The MoGraph toolbar group holds 30 nodes for screen graphics: glitches for broken signals and old screens, transitions between two shots, warps, and shapes, HUD elements and patterns drawn over a background. They're built into Welder and work in proxy and in any tiles the same way.

Glitch

GlitchBlocks, Tear, RGBSplit, PixelSort, SignalLoss, BitCrush and Stutter break a picture apart; CRT, VHS, Hologram and LCDScreen make it look like it's on a screen.

Transitions

WipeTransition (linear, iris, clock, blinds, checker), WarpTransition, GlitchTransition, PixelTransition, ZoomTransition and PushTransition go from A to B over a start frame and length, or follow a progress knob.

Shapes and HUD

Shape (with trim to draw it on), Bars, BoxGrid, Radar, Waveform and Scatter build interface graphics; FlowLines, PatternGrid, NoisePattern and CodeRain fill screens with motion.

Warps

WaveWarp, Bulge and SliceShift bend and cut the picture, animated by their speed knobs.

Random choices are seeded: change seed for a different pattern, and changes per second for how often it re-rolls. Generators draw over their bg input; over bg sets how (over, add, screen, under). For a screen insert, finish with LCDScreen to give the picture real pixels up close.

Round trips

.nk scripts & OFX

Import

File › Import .nk Script…, drag a .nk onto the window, or copy nodes in a .nk app and CtrlV in Welder. Groups, gizmos, backdrops, expressions, roto, tracks and cameras come across.

Export

File › Export .nk Script…, or copy in Welder and paste in a .nk app. Welder-only nodes arrive as labelled NoOps.

Mapped classes

Kronos and OFlow2 become OFlow, Keylight becomes ScreenKeyer, Bokeh becomes Defocus, Vectorfield becomes OCIOFileTransform.

OFX plugins

Loaded from {{OFXDIR}} and OFX_PLUGIN_PATH; they appear under the OFX button and in Tab search.

Untranslatable nodes pass their input through, show red, and are listed in Messages. Studio defaults (slate art, vendor, your slate gizmo) live in {{CFG}}{{S}}studio.json.

Under the mouse

Keyboard shortcuts

Keys act on the panel under the mouse. Help › Keyboard Shortcuts shows this list inside Welder.

Every node

Node reference

Press Tab over the node graph and type a name to create any of these. Colours match the node colours in the graph; NEW marks nodes added in this build.

When something's off

Settings & troubleshooting

Edit › Preferences holds the cache folder (disk cache, BlenderRender frames, AI job files) with sizes and Clear buttons, the playback RAM cache, Use the GPU, network-drive handling, and the offer to match the project to the first Read.
